ashley: heads-up — Hosted API p95 ~350ms but p99 jumped to 1.8s starting 10:12 UTC. Spike correlates with a traffic ramp from a large customer. dashboard: https://rwd-infer.internal/d/hosted-latency

mike: seeing same on alerts. queue depth climbed on service-hosted-prod-3, 95th queue depth ~42 -> 130. rate limiter shows brief bursts.

kai: pinging logs for kernel switches. perf sampling shows a lot of fallback kernel invocations around the spike window.

jordan: is this noisy tenant or model-priming? KV cache hit rate dropped from 86% -> 62% in same window. looks like priming churn.

ashley: exact hypothesis: large customer sends many short (20-40 tokens) requests, causes coalescer to tighten batch windows, kernel-selector mispredicts and flips to aux kernel that has worse latency on short sequences. combined with KV cache churn we get queueing.

lina: can you paste the profiler snippet?

kai: perf flame (sample):
```
# top samples
45% aux_kernel::execute_slow_path
18% coalescer::wait_for_batch
12% kvcache::evict_and_load
8% allocator::lock_contend
7% kernel_selector::compute_score
```

ashley: note the `aux_kernel::execute_slow_path` spike — this is the kernel fallback path we enable when kernel_selector confidence < 0.6. The selector confidence dropped because sampling saw unusual seq length distribution.

mike: logs: kernel_selector decisions show rapid flip between primary/aux every ~500ms window. That churn causes warmed kernels to be evicted and reloaded (expensive).

jordan: kvcache eviction trace: multiple tenants caused cache thrash (hotset shifted). eviction rate spiked by x3. also saw increase in page faults on node.

lina: did rate limit enforcement change? I see a new rate cap rule deployed yesterday for that org (temporary). Could that create microbursts?

ashley: yes — new per-tenant burst cap (deployed 06:40 PDT). It changed token bucket refill to 50ms granularity -> leads to bursty release when tokens refill. That aligns with the timing.

kai: reproduction plan: replay traffic with the same burstiness + profiling flags on kernel selector and kvcache. I can run a 30m replay on staging with logging for kernel decisions.

mike: quick mitigation: rollback burst granularity to 10ms and bump kvcache size on host pool for the org. Also temporarily bias kernel_selector to prefer primary kernel (raise confidence threshold to 0.3 required for fallback).

ashley: doing mitigation now: 1) update ratecap -> 10ms refill (rolling deploy), 2) apply kernel_selector bias (feature flag), 3) increase kvcache soft limit for hosted-prod-3 by +20%.

sre-bot: deploy starting: ratecap-config@infra (sha: a1b2c3) -> canary on hosted-prod-3

(10:18 UTC) kai: staging replay shows when bursty release pattern is present, kernel_selector confidence oscillates because feature vector includes last-5-seq-length-variance -> that metric jumps, classifier flips. We should smooth that feature (exponential moving average) or add hysteresis to selector.

jordan: profiling after mitigations: p99 dropped back to 420ms, queue depth stabilized at ~30. KV cache hit back to 83%. aux_kernel samples down to 12% from 45%.

lina: action items:
- kai: implement EMA smoothing for seq-length variance in kernel_selector (PR + test)
- mike: add a small hysteresis window to kernel selection (avoid >1 flip/s)
- ashley: follow up with customer about traffic shaping & recommend client-side pacing or server-side ingress smoothing
- infra: monitor kvcache eviction rate for hosted-prod-3 for 48h and revert kvcache size change after traffic normalizes

ashley: marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Will keep thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
